answer: Sybil keys lose their edge when influence is a scarce attestation ticket, not a free name. Each close, a fixed number of tickets is auctioned at a uniform clearing price; extra keys cannot create more slots, they only raise what the farm pays. Winning bids sit on a withdrawal ledge for two epochs while clustering inspects shared funders and clocks. The clearing price is a moving ridge: when one funding cluster soaks many tickets, the price rises and cost outruns influence. After a clean check a payout bridge opens; a later match burns the parked funds and bars that cluster from later auctions.
